board_events.caption: Reactants climb to the activated complex, then fall to products; the catalyst lowers the hump

board_events.text: Reactants climb an energy barrier; the top is the activated complex, or transition state.
Barrier from the reactants is $E_a$ forward; from the products it is $E_a$ reverse.
Threshold energy = activation energy PLUS the reactants' own energy — not merely $E_a$.
If products sit below reactants, forward $E_a$ is smaller and the reaction is exothermic.
A catalyst draws a second, lower hump between the same levels, cutting $E_a$ but leaving $\Delta H$ unchanged.

segments.text: Much of this subtopic is examined through the reaction energy profile, so let us learn to read it.

Here it is: potential energy on the vertical axis, reaction coordinate on the horizontal. Reactants on the left, a hump in the middle, products on the right, with a dashed lower hump for the catalysed path.

The reactants begin at some energy and must climb a barrier to react. The top of the barrier is the activated complex, or transition state, a fleeting, highly unstable cluster in which old bonds are partly broken and new bonds partly formed.
The height of the barrier measured from the reactants is the forward activation energy. Measured from the products, it is the reverse activation energy.

Careful with a common confusion. The threshold energy is the total energy the activated complex sits at, which is the reactants' own energy plus the activation energy. A colliding pair must reach this absolute level, not merely supply E a out of nothing.
The enthalpy change is the difference between product and reactant levels, which equals the forward activation energy minus the reverse activation energy.

So if the products sit below the reactants, the forward barrier is smaller than the reverse and the reaction is exothermic, with delta H negative. If products sit higher, it is endothermic. Either way a barrier must be climbed first: feasibility does not guarantee speed.

Finally the catalyst. It draws a second, lower hump between the same reactant and product levels, routing through a different activated complex. That cuts the activation energy for both directions while leaving delta H and the equilibrium exactly where they were.
इस subtopic का बहुत हिस्सा reaction energy profile से examine होता है, तो चलिए इसे पढ़ना सीखते हैं।
ये रहा, potential energy vertical axis पर, reaction coordinate horizontal पर। बाईं तरफ़ reactants, बीच में एक hump, दाईं तरफ़ products, और catalysed path के लिए एक dashed lower hump।

Reactants किसी energy पर शुरू होते हैं और react करने के लिए एक barrier चढ़ना होता है। Barrier का top activated complex, या transition state है, एक fleeting, बहुत unstable cluster जिसमें पुराने bonds partly टूटे और नए bonds partly बने होते हैं।
Reactants से मापी barrier की height forward activation energy है। Products से मापें तो reverse activation energy।

एक common confusion से सावधान। Threshold energy वो total energy है जिस पर activated complex बैठा है, यानी reactants की अपनी energy plus activation energy। एक colliding pair को इस absolute level तक पहुँचना है, सिर्फ़ E a शून्य से पैदा नहीं करना।
Enthalpy change product और reactant levels का अंतर है, जो forward activation energy minus reverse activation energy के बराबर है।

तो अगर products reactants से नीचे बैठें, forward barrier reverse से छोटा है और reaction exothermic है, delta H negative। Products ऊपर हों तो endothermic। किसी भी हाल में barrier पहले चढ़ना है, feasibility speed की guarantee नहीं देती।

आख़िर में catalyst। वो उन्हीं reactant और product levels के बीच एक दूसरा, नीचा hump खींचता है, एक अलग activated complex से route करते हुए। इससे दोनों directions की activation energy कटती है जबकि delta H और equilibrium ठीक वहीं रहते हैं।

sections.title: Collision Theory and Arrhenius: The Formula Set

board_events.text: Consolidated formulas for this subtopic

board_events.latex: k = A\,e^{-E_a/RT}, \quad \ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{RT}, \quad \log k = \log A - \frac{E_a}{2.303\,RT}

board_events.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 460 300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif"><rect x="0" y="0" width="460" height="180" fill="#ffffff"/><text x="230" y="34" fill="#111111" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">k = A e⁻ᴴᵀₒᴸᵗ</text><rect x="30" y="55" width="180" height="95" rx="8" fill="#f6f8fa" stroke="#8c959f"/><text x="120" y="80" fill="#111111" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">ln k = ln A − Eᵢ/RT</text><text x="120" y="108" fill="#d1242f" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">slope −Eᵢ/R</text><text x="120" y="128" fill="#111111" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">vs 1/T</text><rect x="250" y="55" width="180" height="95" rx="8" fill="#f6f8fa" stroke="#8c959f"/><text x="340" y="80" fill="#111111" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">log(k₂/k₁) =</text><text x="340" y="102" fill="#111111" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">(Eᵢ/2.303R)</text><text x="340" y="124" fill="#111111" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">×(T₂−T₁)/(T₁T₂)</text></svg>
board_events.caption: Graphical and two-temperature forms of the Arrhenius equation

board_events.text: Temperature coefficient $= k_{(t+10)}/k_t$, typically between 2 and 3.

segments.text: Here is the consolidated formula set for collision theory and temperature dependence.

The Arrhenius equation and its working forms. k equals A times e to the minus E a over R T. Take logs: natural log of k equals log A minus E a over R T, and in base ten, log k equals log A minus E a over two point three zero three R T.
The panel shows the two most useful forms for problems: the straight-line graph and the two-temperature relation.
The two-temperature form: log of k two over k one equals E a over two point three zero three R, times the quantity T two minus T one over T one T two. This eliminates A.
The energy relationships. Threshold energy equals the activation energy plus the reactants' own energy. And the forward activation energy minus the reverse activation energy equals delta H.
The collision-theory rate: P times Z A B times e to the minus E a over R T, with the pre-exponential factor A equal to P times Z A B.
The temperature coefficient is the ratio of the rate constant ten degrees higher to the rate constant now, and it typically lies between two and three.
And the graphical route: a plot of natural log of k against one over T has slope minus E a over R, while using log k the slope is minus E a over two point three zero three R.
ये रहा collision theory और temperature dependence का consolidated formula set।

Arrhenius equation और उसके working forms। k बराबर A times e to the minus E a over R T। Logs लीजिए, natural log of k बराबर log A minus E a over R T, और base ten में, log k बराबर log A minus E a over two point three zero three R T।
Panel problems के लिए दो सबसे useful forms दिखाता है, straight-line graph और two-temperature relation।
Two-temperature form, log of k two over k one बराबर E a over two point three zero three R, times the quantity T two minus T one over T one T two। ये A eliminate करता है।
Energy relationships। Threshold energy बराबर activation energy plus reactants की अपनी energy। और forward activation energy minus reverse activation energy बराबर delta H।
Collision-theory rate, P times Z A B times e to the minus E a over R T, जिसमें pre-exponential factor A बराबर P times Z A B।
Temperature coefficient है दस degree ऊपर के rate constant और अभी के rate constant का ratio, और ये typically दो और तीन के बीच होता है।
और graphical route, natural log of k को one over T के against plot की slope minus E a over R है, जबकि log k use करें तो slope minus E a over two point three zero three R।

sections.title: Activation Energy from Two Rate Constants (CBSE)

board_events.text: CBSE: $k$ rises from $3.0\times10^{-4}$ to $1.2\times10^{-3}\,\text{s}^{-1}$

board_events.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 460 300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif"><rect x="0" y="0" width="460" height="200" fill="#ffffff"/><text x="230" y="28" fill="#111111" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">k₂/k₁ = (1.2×10⁻³)/(3.0×10⁻⁴) = 4</text><text x="230" y="62" fill="#111111" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">T₁ = 300 K,  T₂ = 320 K,  log 4 = 0.602</text><text x="230" y="98" fill="#111111" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">bracket = (320−300)/(300×320) = 2.083×10⁻⁴</text><rect x="90" y="118" width="280" height="46" rx="8" fill="#f6f8fa" stroke="#1a7f37" stroke-width="2"/><text x="230" y="146" fill="#1a7f37" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Eᵢ ≈ 55.3 kJ mol⁻¹</text></svg>
board_events.caption: Feed the ratio and the two temperatures into the two-temperature form

board_events.text: The rate constant ratio is $1.2\times10^{-3}$ over $3.0\times10^{-4}$, which is 4.
The bracket is 20 over 96000, which is $2.083\times10^{-4}$.
Two rate-constant, temperature pairs are exactly enough to eliminate $A$ and solve for $E_a$.

segments.text: First worked example of subtopic four, C B S E board level. A first-order reaction has rate constant three point zero times ten to the minus four per second at three hundred kelvin, rising to one point two times ten to the minus three per second at three hundred twenty kelvin. Find the activation energy.
The picture lays out the plug-in: the ratio is four, the temperatures are three hundred and three hundred twenty, and log four is zero point six zero two.
First the ratio. k two over k one is one point two times ten to the minus three, over three point zero times ten to the minus four, which is four.

Substitute into the two-temperature form. Log four equals E a over two point three zero three times eight point three one four, times the bracket three hundred twenty minus three hundred, over three hundred times three hundred twenty.
Evaluate the bracket. Twenty over ninety six thousand is two point zero eight three times ten to the minus four per kelvin.

Now solve for E a. It equals two point three zero three, times eight point three one four, times zero point six zero two, all divided by two point zero eight three times ten to the minus four. That comes to about fifty five point three kilojoules per mole.
The takeaway: two rate-constant and temperature pairs are exactly enough to eliminate the unknown A and solve cleanly for the activation energy.

Subtopic four का पहला worked example, C B S E board level। एक first-order reaction का rate constant तीन सौ kelvin पर तीन point zero into ten to the minus four per second है, जो तीन सौ बीस kelvin पर बढ़कर एक point दो into ten to the minus three per second हो जाता है। Activation energy निकालिए।
Picture plug-in बताती है, ratio चार है, temperatures तीन सौ और तीन सौ बीस हैं, और log four zero point six zero two है।
पहले ratio। k two over k one है एक point दो into ten to the minus three, over तीन point zero into ten to the minus four, यानी चार।
Two-temperature form में substitute कीजिए। Log four बराबर E a over two point three zero three into eight point three one four, times the bracket तीन सौ बीस minus तीन सौ, over तीन सौ into तीन सौ बीस।
Bracket evaluate कीजिए। बीस over छियानवे हज़ार है दो point zero आठ तीन into ten to the minus four per kelvin।

अब E a के लिए solve कीजिए। ये बराबर two point three zero three, times eight point three one four, times zero point six zero two, सब divided by दो point zero आठ तीन into ten to the minus four। ये आता है लगभग पचपन point तीन kilojoules per mole।
Takeaway, दो rate-constant और temperature pairs unknown A को eliminate करके activation energy के लिए साफ़ solve करने को बिल्कुल पर्याप्त हैं।

sections.title: The Temperature-Coefficient Shortcut (NEET)

board_events.text: NEET: rate goes 4-fold from 27 to 47 degrees; what from 27 to 57?

board_events.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 460 300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif"><rect x="0" y="0" width="460" height="220" fill="#ffffff"/><text x="230" y="28" fill="#111111" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Count 10°C intervals, raise to that power</text><text x="60" y="70" fill="#111111" font-size="13">27 → 47°C = two intervals, rate ×4</text><text x="60" y="98" fill="#1f6feb" font-size="13">→ coefficient = √4 = 2 per 10°C</text><text x="60" y="132" fill="#111111" font-size="13">27 → 57°C = three intervals</text><rect x="120" y="150" width="220" height="46" rx="8" fill="#f6f8fa" stroke="#1a7f37" stroke-width="2"/><text x="230" y="178" fill="#1a7f37" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">factor = 2³ = 8</text></svg>
board_events.caption: Count 10-degree intervals, then raise the coefficient to that power

board_events.text: From 27 to 47 degrees is two 10-degree intervals, and the rate quadruples.
From 27 to 57 degrees is three intervals.
The coefficient is multiplicative per interval, never additive — count intervals, raise to the power.

segments.text: Second example, a N E E T speed trap that rewards a shortcut. The rate becomes four times faster when the temperature rises from twenty seven to forty seven degrees Celsius. Assuming a constant temperature coefficient, what factor applies from twenty seven to fifty seven degrees?
The ladder on the board is the method: count how many ten-degree steps you climb, then raise the per-step coefficient to that power.
From twenty seven to forty seven is two ten-degree intervals, and over those the rate quadruples, a factor of four.
So the per-ten-degree coefficient is the square root of four, which is two.
Now the target jump. From twenty seven to fifty seven is three ten-degree intervals.
So the factor is two cubed, which is eight. That is the answer.

The trap: students reach for the full Arrhenius equation and waste time, or add instead of multiply and answer six. The coefficient is multiplicative per interval, never additive. Count the intervals and raise to that power.

दूसरा example, एक N E E T speed trap जो shortcut को reward करता है। Rate चार गुना तेज़ हो जाती है जब temperature सत्ताईस से सैंतालीस degree Celsius तक बढ़ती है। Constant temperature coefficient मानते हुए, सत्ताईस से सत्तावन degree तक कौन-सा factor लगता है?
Board पर ladder ही method है, गिनिए कि आप कितने दस-degree steps चढ़ते हैं, फिर per-step coefficient को उस power तक raise कीजिए।
सत्ताईस से सैंतालीस दो दस-degree intervals हैं, और उन पर rate चार गुना, factor of four।
तो per-ten-degree coefficient है square root of four, यानी दो।
अब target jump। सत्ताईस से सत्तावन तीन दस-degree intervals हैं।
तो factor है two cubed, यानी आठ। यही answer है।

Trap, students full Arrhenius equation उठाकर time बर्बाद करते हैं, या multiply की जगह add करके छह answer देते हैं। Coefficient per interval multiplicative है, कभी additive नहीं। Intervals गिनिए और उस power तक raise कीजिए।

sections.title: From Graph Slope to Boltzmann Fraction (JEE Main)

board_events.text: JEE Main: $\ln k$ vs $1/T$ has slope $-1.2\times10^{4}$ K

board_events.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 460 300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif"><rect x="0" y="0" width="460" height="220" fill="#ffffff"/><text x="230" y="28" fill="#111111" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">ln k vs 1/T: slope = −1.2×10⁴ K</text><text x="230" y="62" fill="#111111" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">Eᵢ = −slope × R = (1.2×10⁴)(8.314) ≈ 99.8 kJ mol⁻¹</text><text x="230" y="98" fill="#111111" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">Eᵢ/RT = 9.98×10⁴ / (8.314×300) ≈ 40.0</text><rect x="90" y="118" width="280" height="46" rx="8" fill="#f6f8fa" stroke="#d1242f" stroke-width="2"/><text x="230" y="146" fill="#d1242f" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">fraction = e⁻⁴⁰ ≈ 4.2×10⁻¹⁸</text><text x="230" y="192" fill="#9a6700" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">fewer than one in 10¹⁷ are energetic enough</text></svg>
board_events.caption: The slope gives Ea; the Boltzmann factor gives the reacting fraction

board_events.text: (a) Slope $= -E_a/R$, so $E_a = -\text{slope}\times R$.
(b) The Boltzmann fraction is $f = e^{-E_a/RT}$ at 300 K.
Fewer than one in $10^{17}$ molecules are energetic enough — which is why the reaction is slow.

segments.text: Third example, J E E Main, linking a graph to physics. A plot of natural log of k against one over T is a straight line of slope minus one point two times ten to the four kelvin.
The picture carries both halves: from the slope to the activation energy, and from there to the tiny reacting fraction.
Part a. For an Arrhenius plot the slope equals minus E a over R, so the activation energy is minus the slope times R.
Numerically, one point two times ten to the four, times eight point three one four, is about ninety nine point eight kilojoules per mole. A high barrier.
Part b asks for the fraction of molecules with energy at least E a at three hundred kelvin. That fraction is the Boltzmann factor, e to the minus E a over R T.

Compute the exponent. E a over R T is ninety nine point eight thousand over eight point three one four times three hundred, which is about forty. So the fraction is e to the minus forty, roughly four point two times ten to the minus eighteen.

That means fewer than one in ten to the seventeen molecules are energetic enough at three hundred kelvin, which is exactly why this high-barrier reaction is slow, and why heating it helps so dramatically. The skill is linking the graphical slope to the physical Maxwell-Boltzmann fraction.
तीसरा example, J E E Main, एक graph को physics से जोड़ता है। Natural log of k को one over T के against एक सीधी line है जिसकी slope minus एक point दो into ten to the four kelvin है।
Picture दोनों halves ले जाती है, slope से activation energy तक, और वहाँ से tiny reacting fraction तक।
Part a। Arrhenius plot के लिए slope बराबर minus E a over R, तो activation energy है minus the slope times R।
Numerically, एक point दो into ten to the four, times eight point three one four, है लगभग निन्यानवे point आठ kilojoules per mole। एक high barrier।
Part b तीन सौ kelvin पर कम-से-कम E a energy वाले molecules का fraction पूछता है। वो fraction है Boltzmann factor, e to the minus E a over R T।

Exponent compute कीजिए। E a over R T है निन्यानवे point आठ हज़ार over eight point three one four into तीन सौ, यानी लगभग चालीस। तो fraction है e to the minus चालीस, मोटे तौर पर चार point दो into ten to the minus eighteen।

इसका मतलब तीन सौ kelvin पर दस to the seventeen में से एक से भी कम molecule energetic है, ठीक इसीलिए ये high-barrier reaction slow है, और heating इतना dramatically मदद करती है। Skill graphical slope को physical Maxwell-Boltzmann fraction से जोड़ना है।

board_events.text: JEE Advanced: $E_a$ drops from 90 to 60 kJ per mole

board_events.caption: Same A and T: the rate ratio is the exponential of the barrier reduction over RT

board_events.text: The barrier drop is 90 minus 60, which is 30 kilojoules per mole.
A 30 kJ reduction multiplies the rate roughly 170,000-fold — the exponential leverage of $E_a$.
The catalyst leaves $\Delta H$ and $K_{eq}$ unchanged; it helps both directions equally.

segments.text: Fourth example, J E E Advanced, quantifying a catalyst. At three hundred kelvin a catalyst lowers the activation energy from ninety to sixty kilojoules per mole, with the pre-exponential factor A essentially unchanged. By what factor does the rate constant increase?
The picture shows the setup and the striking result: a modest barrier cut buys an enormous speed-up.
Write Arrhenius for the catalysed and uncatalysed paths with the same A and the same T. The ratio k catalysed over k uncatalysed is e to the difference of the two activation energies, over R T.
The barrier drop is ninety minus sixty, which is thirty kilojoules per mole, or three times ten to the four joules per mole.
So the ratio is e to the thirty thousand over eight point three one four times three hundred, which is e to the twelve point zero three, about one point seven times ten to the five.
That is a jump of roughly one hundred seventy thousand fold, all from a thirty kilojoule reduction in the barrier. A vivid demonstration of the exponential leverage of the activation energy.

As for the enthalpy: the catalyst lowers both the forward and reverse barriers by routing through a different activated complex, so it leaves the reactant and product energies, and hence delta H and the equilibrium constant, completely unchanged.

चौथा example, J E E Advanced, एक catalyst को quantify करता है। तीन सौ kelvin पर एक catalyst activation energy को नब्बे से साठ kilojoules per mole तक lower करता है, pre-exponential factor A essentially unchanged के साथ। Rate constant किस factor से बढ़ता है?
Picture setup दिखाती है और चौंकाने वाला result, एक modest barrier cut एक enormous speed-up ख़रीदता है।
Catalysed और uncatalysed paths के लिए Arrhenius same A और same T के साथ लिखिए। Ratio k catalysed over k uncatalysed है e to the difference of the two activation energies, over R T।
Barrier drop है नब्बे minus साठ, यानी तीस kilojoules per mole, या तीन into ten to the four joules per mole।
तो ratio है e to the तीस हज़ार over eight point three one four into तीन सौ, यानी e to the बारह point zero तीन, लगभग एक point सात into ten to the five।
ये लगभग एक लाख सत्तर हज़ार गुना का jump है, सब सिर्फ़ तीस kilojoule barrier reduction से। Activation energy के exponential leverage का जीवंत demonstration।

Enthalpy की बात, catalyst forward और reverse दोनों barriers को एक अलग activated complex से route करके lower करता है, तो reactant और product energies, और इसलिए delta H और equilibrium constant, बिल्कुल unchanged छोड़ता है।

sections.title: Collision Theory: Pitfalls and Pro-Tips

board_events.text: The four traps that cost marks
Thinking a catalyst changes $\Delta H$ or shifts equilibrium — it does neither.
It lowers $E_a$ for both directions equally: rate up, but $\Delta H$, $K_{eq}$ and yield untouched.
Sign slips in the two-temperature form — with $T_2 \gt T_1$ you must get $k_2 \gt k_1$.
If your $E_a$ comes out negative, you swapped $T_1$ and $T_2$ inside the bracket.
Confusing threshold energy with activation energy: threshold is $E_a$ plus the reactants' energy.
Assuming every energetic collision reacts — orientation matters too, hence the steric factor.
Pro-tip: for temperature jumps, count 10-degree intervals; for $E_a$ from a graph, slope times $R$, flip the sign.

segments.text: Let us close subtopic four with the four traps that reliably cost marks.
First and most tempting: thinking a catalyst changes delta H or shifts the equilibrium. It does neither.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy for both directions equally. The rate goes up, but delta H, the equilibrium constant, and the product yield are all untouched.
Second, sign slips in the two-temperature form. With T two greater than T one, you must end up with k two greater than k one.
So if your activation energy comes out negative, you have swapped T one and T two inside the bracket. Fix the order and the sign corrects itself.
Third, confusing threshold energy with activation energy. Threshold energy is the activation energy plus the energy the reactants already possess. E a is only the extra hump on top.
Fourth, assuming every energetic collision reacts. Orientation matters too. That is the whole point of the steric factor: energy is necessary but not sufficient.

<whisper> And the pro-tips. For rate-changes-by-what-factor questions, never reach for Arrhenius; count the ten degree intervals and raise the coefficient to that power. For E a from a graph, remember slope times R, then flip the sign.
चलिए subtopic four को उन चार traps के साथ बंद करते हैं जो reliably marks खाते हैं।
पहला और सबसे tempting, ये सोचना कि catalyst delta H बदलता है या equilibrium shift करता है। वो दोनों में से कुछ नहीं करता।
Catalyst activation energy को दोनों directions के लिए बराबर lower करता है। Rate ऊपर जाती है, पर delta H, equilibrium constant, और product yield सब untouched रहते हैं।
दूसरा, two-temperature form में sign slips। T two के T one से बड़े होने पर, आपको k two, k one से बड़ा मिलना ही चाहिए।
तो अगर आपकी activation energy negative आए, तो आपने bracket के अंदर T one और T two swap कर दिए हैं। Order ठीक कीजिए और sign अपने आप सुधर जाता है।
तीसरा, threshold energy को activation energy से confuse करना। Threshold energy है activation energy plus वो energy जो reactants के पास पहले से है। E a सिर्फ़ ऊपर का extra hump है।
चौथा, ये मानना कि हर energetic collision react करती है। Orientation भी मायने रखती है। यही steric factor का पूरा point है, energy necessary है पर sufficient नहीं।

<whisper> और pro-tips। rate किस factor से बदलती है वाले सवालों के लिए कभी Arrhenius मत उठाइए, दस degree intervals गिनिए और coefficient को उस power तक raise कीजिए। Graph से E a के लिए, slope times R, फिर sign flip कीजिए।

segments.text: Here is your complete kinetics toolkit, gathered on one board. This is a recap, so we are restating, not re-teaching. Consider it your revision map for the whole chapter.
The map has four pillars: rate and order, the integrated equations, pseudo first order, and Arrhenius. Everything you need sits in these four boxes.
Pillar one, rate and order. Rate equals k times A to the x, B to the y. The overall order n is x plus y. And the units of k are mol to the one minus n, litre to the n minus one, per second.

Pillar two, the integrated equations. Zero order: concentration equals R naught minus k t, with half-life R naught over two k. First order: k equals two point three zero three over t, times log of R naught over R, with half-life zero point six nine three over k.
The gas-phase first-order form, for A giving B plus C: k equals two point three zero three over t, times log of p i over the quantity two p i minus p t.
Pillar three, pseudo first order. The observed constant k prime equals k times the excess concentration, and the half-life is zero point six nine three over k prime.

Pillar four, Arrhenius. k equals A times e to the minus E a over R T, and the two-temperature form, log of k two over k one equals E a over two point three zero three R, times T two minus T one over T one T two.

And two graphical fingerprints to keep at hand: the order comes from the slope of log half-life against log starting concentration, which is one minus n, and the activation energy comes from the slope of natural log of k against one over T.
ये रहा आपका complete kinetics toolkit, एक board पर इकट्ठा। ये एक recap है, तो हम restate कर रहे हैं, दोबारा नहीं पढ़ा रहे। इसे पूरे chapter का revision नक़्शा समझिए।
नक़्शे में चार pillars हैं, rate और order, integrated equations, pseudo first order, और Arrhenius। जो भी चाहिए इन चार boxes में बैठा है।
Pillar one, rate और order। Rate बराबर k times A to the x, B to the y। Overall order n है x plus y। और k की units हैं mol to the one minus n, litre to the n minus one, per second।

Pillar two, integrated equations। Zero order, concentration बराबर R naught minus k t, half-life R naught over two k के साथ। First order, k बराबर two point three zero three over t, times log of R naught over R, half-life zero point six nine three over k के साथ।
Gas-phase first-order form, A देता है B plus C के लिए, k बराबर two point three zero three over t, times log of p i over the quantity two p i minus p t।
Pillar three, pseudo first order। Observed constant k prime बराबर k times excess concentration, और half-life zero point six nine three over k prime।

Pillar four, Arrhenius। k बराबर A times e to the minus E a over R T, और two-temperature form, log of k two over k one बराबर E a over two point three zero three R, times T two minus T one over T one T two।

और दो graphical fingerprints हाथ में रखिए, order आता है log half-life को log starting concentration के against की slope से, जो one minus n है, और activation energy आती है natural log of k को one over T के against की slope से।

board_events.text: Order is observed (may be 0, fractional, negative); molecularity is counted (1, 2 or 3, elementary only).
Units of $k$: order 0 gives mol per litre per second; order 1, per second; order 2, litre per mole per second.
Half-life: first order ignores $[R]_0$; zero order is proportional to $[R]_0$; second order goes as $1/[R]_0$.
First-order ladder: 50% is 1 half-life, 75% is 2, 87.5% is 3, and 99.9% is about 10.

segments.text: And finally the cheat sheet, the fast-recall box to run through just before the exam. Short, sharp, and lifted straight from the chapter's own quick-recall boxes.
The memory aids on the board anchor everything: order versus molecularity, the half-life rules, the log pairing, and the catalyst.

Order versus molecularity. Order is observed and may be zero, fractional, or negative. Molecularity is counted, a whole number one, two, or three, and only for elementary steps. Order is observed, molecularity is mechanistic.
Units of k by order. Order zero is mol per litre per second, order one is per second, order two is litre per mole per second. The units double as a check on your order.
The half-life rules. First order forgets the start, so the half-life ignores the starting concentration. Zero order is proportional to it, and second order goes as one over it.

The first-order completion ladder. Fifty percent is one half-life, seventy five percent is two, eighty seven point five percent is three, and ninety nine point nine percent is about ten. Count halvings before you touch a calculator.
Pseudo first order in one line: molecularity two, observed order one, with k prime equal to k times the excess. And keep two point three zero three paired with log or lose the marks.

And collision theory in one breath: a collision reacts only with enough energy and the right orientation. A catalyst cuts the climb, the activation energy, but never the cliff, the enthalpy change. Go get those marks.
और आख़िर में cheat sheet, exam से ठीक पहले दौड़ाने वाला fast-recall box। छोटा, तेज़, और सीधे chapter के अपने quick-recall boxes से लिया हुआ।
Board पर memory aids सब कुछ anchor करते हैं, order versus molecularity, half-life rules, log pairing, और catalyst।

Order versus molecularity। Order observed है और zero, fractional, या negative हो सकता है। Molecularity counted है, whole number एक, दो, या तीन, और सिर्फ़ elementary steps के लिए। Order observed है, molecularity mechanistic है।
Units of k by order। Order zero है mol per litre per second, order one per second, order two litre per mole per second। Units आपके order का check भी हैं।
Half-life rules। First order start भूल जाती है, तो half-life starting concentration ignore करती है। Zero order उसके proportional है, और second order one over उसके जाती है।
First-order completion ladder। पचास percent एक half-life, पचहत्तर percent दो, साढ़े सत्तासी percent तीन, और निन्यानवे point नौ percent लगभग दस। Calculator छूने से पहले halvings गिनिए।
Pseudo first order एक line में, molecularity दो, observed order एक, k prime बराबर k times excess के साथ। और two point three zero three को log के साथ pair रखिए या marks खोइए।

और collision theory एक साँस में, एक collision तभी react करती है जब energy पर्याप्त हो और orientation सही। Catalyst climb, यानी activation energy, काटता है, पर cliff, यानी enthalpy change, कभी नहीं। जाइए वो marks ले आइए।
